stories.headline: Designing an AI serving harness built to last
stories.summary: The next competitive advantage in enterprise AI has less to do with which model you choose than with what you build around it. For the past several years, much of the AI conversation has centered on model capability: bigger models, better reasoning, larger context windows, higher benchmark scores.
stories.why_it_matters: Those advances have been extraordinary. This marks a notable development for engineering teams working in ai & machine learning.
key_points: Problem & Context: The next competitive advantage in enterprise AI has less to do with which model you choose than with what you build around it.
Technical Implementation: For the past several years, much of the AI conversation has centered on model capability: bigger models, better reasoning, larger context windows, higher benchmark scores.

Deployment & Impact: But as AI moves from experimentation to production, the question facing enterprise leaders has changed—it’s no longer, “what can the model do?”—it’s now, “Can we deliver that intelligence reliably, economically, and at scale?” Increasingly, the answer depends on the serving harness—the engineering system surrounding the model, including the architecture, memory management , scheduling, and optimization decisions that determine how efficiently model intelligence becomes a production capability.

stories.headline: Switch 2 security takes a hit as hackers unlock homebrew access
stories.summary: A security researcher has demonstrated a software-only partial jailbreak of the Switch 2, gaining "userland" access that he says "lets us run homebrew, reverse engineer and mod Switch 2 games, back up save files off the Switch, and access most of the Switch 2’s peripherals through MMIO." The hack relies on the original Switch version of SmileBasic 4 , the latest in a long-running series of programming environments and interpreters that run on Nintendo hardware. The so-called "tethered" hack also requires access to a macOS or Linux PC on the same network to run a node.js package that helps enable privileged system access.
stories.why_it_matters: Researcher Sammy Hajhamid writes that he used OpenAI's Codex to poke at SmileBasic's language interpreter, using a custom harness that could send USB commands to the system and view results via HDMI (as well as power cycling via a Bluetooth light switch flipping device). This marks a notable development for engineering teams working in developers.

stories.headline: The Thin Orchestrator: How We Made Our AI Agents More Reliable by Giving the Router Less to Do
stories.summary: Skip to content Search this site Open Source Platforms Infrastructure Systems Physical Infrastructure Video Engineering & AR/VR Artificial Intelligence Watch Videos POSTED ON OCTOBER 19, 2026 TO AI RESEARCH, ML APPLICATIONS The Thin Orchestrator: How We Made Our AI Agents More Reliable by Giving the Router Less to Do By Plawan Rath, Akhil Jindal, Ashwini Verma Sometimes, giving an AI agent all of the knowledge it needs is the wrong approach. At Meta, we’ve seen notable improvements in efficiency and accuracy by keeping the orchestration layer of our data pipeline agents deliberately thin: It routes work and enforces reliability checks, while specialized agents do the domain reasoning.
stories.why_it_matters: We’re sharing our own process and insights, plus how any team can apply this to their production AI agents. This marks a notable development for engineering teams working in big tech.

Technical Implementation: At Meta, we’ve seen notable improvements in efficiency and accuracy by keeping the orchestration layer of our data pipeline agents deliberately thin: It routes work and enforces reliability checks, while specialized agents do the domain reasoning.

stories.headline: Single-tenant Titus: VM-level isolation on a multi-tenant container platform
stories.summary: Samartha Chandrashekar & Nick Parker You click play on a Friday night, and in the second that follows, dozens of services answer in milliseconds. Most of them run on Titus, our internal container platform.
stories.why_it_matters: Titus is, in essence, a Kubernetes-based container hosting platform: we keep both the control plane and the data plane (the container hosts that actually run containers) patched and up to date, so application teams get a consistent and reliable container experience. This marks a notable development for engineering teams working in big tech.
key_points: Problem & Context: Titus is, in essence, a Kubernetes-based container hosting platform: we keep both the control plane and the data plane (the container hosts that actually run containers) patched and up to date, so application teams get a consistent and reliable container experience.
Technical Implementation: For a few, it does not, and those few include some of the most demanding real-time systems we run.

Deployment & Impact: This post is about them, and about single-tenant Titus, a mode that gives a task its own virtual machine while keeping everything else about Titus the same: the API, the deployment path, and the managed experience where the Compute/Platform team, not the application team, owns the host.

stories.summary: When platform teams manage containerized applications at scale on Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) , configuring ingress networking for each service often becomes a bottleneck. stories.why_it_matters: This per-service overhead slows down deployment velocity and increases the risk of configuration drift across an organization. This marks a notable development for engineering teams working in cloud.

stories.headline: Introducing full transaction detection for Cloudflare WAF
stories.summary: Today, we are expanding our web application firewall (WAF) by adding two new capabilities: full transaction detections and response rules. Full transaction detections evaluate each HTTP request alongside its response to identify evidence of exploitation.
stories.why_it_matters: It helps answer both "Does this request look malicious?" and "What happened when the application handled it?" Response rules can then block the origin’s response before it reaches the requester. This marks a notable development for engineering teams working in cloud.
key_points: Problem & Context: These are valuable protections because the latest frontier models are uncovering vulnerabilities buried deep in widely used software, giving defenders clarity on what to fix — and attackers new paths to exploit.
Technical Implementation: With these new capabilities, customers can use Cloudflare-managed protections or build their own policies combining request and response properties.
Deployment & Impact: This extends our always-on application security framework, with detection results available in Security Analytics to support investigation.

stories.headline: A Small Model Asks Better: Fine-Tuning Query Clarification for Retrieval-Augmented Generation
stories.summary: arXiv:2610.28686v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Query clarification is essential for retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems that face ambiguous user queries. We consider multi-turn grounded conversational scenarios where a user query is either ill-formed or ambiguous in the context of the prior dialog or, more interestingly, it may be well-formed but when posed against retrieved documents there are multiple relevant interpretations.
stories.why_it_matters: The task is to recognize both such cases and then generate an appropriate clarification request to the user. This marks a notable development for engineering teams working in technology research.
key_points: Problem & Context: arXiv:2610.28686v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Query clarification is essential for retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems that face ambiguous user queries.
Technical Implementation: We present ClariEdge, a new dataset of approximately 3,900 examples that include such ambiguous queries along with negative examples that do not require clarification.

Deployment & Impact: We also show that a lightweight fine-tuned LoRA achieves 96.6% classification accuracy and outperforms prompted baselines of many larger models on both classification and quality of clarification generation.

stories.headline: Scaling in Games: Continued Pre-Training For Embodied Agents In Diverse Virtual Worlds
stories.summary: arXiv:2610.28698v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Scaling data, diversity and model capacity has improved embodied learning in physical environments, where diverse experiences remain grounded in shared physical laws. Whether these gains extend to virtual worlds with different visual styles, dynamics, controls, and objectives remains unclear.
stories.why_it_matters: We investigate this question through a controlled study of continued pre-training (CPT) across three axes: data volume, diversity, and model size. This marks a notable development for engineering teams working in technology research.
key_points: Problem & Context: arXiv:2610.28698v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Scaling data, diversity and model capacity has improved embodied learning in physical environments, where diverse experiences remain grounded in shared physical laws.
Technical Implementation: We investigate this question through a controlled study of continued pre-training (CPT) across three axes: data volume, diversity, and model size.

Deployment & Impact: Our 120 training configurations span four model sizes from 0.8B to 27B, six data budgets from 50 to 1,600 hours, and five mixtures ranging from Minecraft-only data to diverse multi-world corpora.
